items.a: Prompt = **one answer**. Loop = **recursive goal** you define once: run → self-check against **stop condition** → repeat or exit. Optional **max iterations** (e.g. 10) as a safety rail.

items.q: When should you loop vs prompt?
items.a: **Looping ≠ replacing prompting yet.** Greenfield features → still prompt (Claude Code). Daily **repeatable ops** with clear done-criteria → loop.

items.q: What did the Sentry and CloudWatch loops do?
items.a: Sentry: pull unresolved BridgeSpace errors → dedupe → prioritize → fix → push. Stop: **no unresolved high-priority** issues → shipped **BridgeSpace v3.4**. CloudWatch: AWS errors until **none require code changes**.

items.q: How do PostHog and Semrush loops use external data?
items.a: PostHog: conversion opportunities → GitHub edits; stop = reviewed + **≥3 data-backed improvements**. Semrush: SEO fixes → tests/builds pass → deploy; creates a **PR on completion**.

items.q: Can multiple loops run at once?
items.a: Yes — demo ran **seven parallel loops** (SEO, Sentry, CloudWatch, PostHog, others); one already shipped a BridgeSpace update mid-demo.

items.q: What makes a task a good loop candidate?
items.a: Tasks with **verifiable external state** as stop signal: Sentry/CloudWatch error triage, PostHog conversion work, Semrush SEO — not open-ended greenfield design.

items.q: What's BridgeAgent's moat vs Claude Code/Codex?
items.a: Claude/Codex are **harnesses**; BridgeAgent positions as an **autonomous software developer** with native GitHub, Sentry, Cloudflare, PostHog, Semrush, AWS. `/goal` exists on harnesses but lacks the integrated observability stack.

items.q: What human work does looping eliminate?
items.a: Manual Claude Sentry ritual (MCP pull → table → plan → execute → push) becomes **one-click**. "I'll never have to write that prompt again" for work you do **every single day**.
